title: Concurrent and Successive Plans of Care Under Outpatient and Part B Therapy Services
content:
Under **Outpatient and Part B Therapy Services**, a therapy referral is registered as a plan of care for the resident. The plan is registered with the resident, the tier set from the payer and the discipline, and the referral date (the date of the order for evaluation), and it begins in the referred status.

## Rule

> A resident may have several therapy plans at once, one per discipline, and successive plans over time. A new plan is opened only when the resident has no other plan of the same tier that is referred, active or on hold.

In the records' own words, the statuses that stand in the way of a new plan of the same tier are **referred**, **active** and **on hold**. There is no fixed limit on the total number of plans a resident may hold; the limit the rule sets is per tier, by status.

## What the condition is judged on

- **Evidence.** The condition is judged on the system's record of the resident's existing plans of care — each plan's tier and status — as it stands before the new plan is opened. A caller's account of what plans exist does not replace the record.
- **Object.** The plans compared are those of the same resident, and only those in the same tier as the plan to be opened.

## Decision table (another plan of the same resident)

| The other plan's tier | The other plan's status | Effect of the condition on opening the new plan |
|---|---|---|
| Same tier | Referred | Not opened |
| Same tier | Active | Not opened |
| Same tier | On hold | Not opened |
| Same tier | Discharged, closed or not indicated | The condition does not stand in the way |
| A different tier | Any status | The condition does not stand in the way |

## Illustrations (hypothetical residents)

- A resident has an active Medicare Part B Physical Therapy Plan of Care. A new referral for occupational therapy under Medicare Part B falls in a different tier, the Medicare Part B Occupational Therapy Plan of Care, so the two plans may run at once.
- A resident's earlier Private Pay Therapy Plan of Care was discharged and closed some months ago. A new Private Pay Therapy Plan of Care referral is not blocked by that closed plan: successive plans over time are allowed.
- A resident's Medicare Part B Speech-Language Pathology Plan of Care is on hold. A further plan in that same tier is not opened while the existing one is referred, active or on hold.
